newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end firmer as yen dips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end firmer as yen dips.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures closed firmer on Monday, supported by the yen's weakening against the dollar and firmer LME prices last Friday, traders said.
TOCOM aluminium ended 1.5 to 2.7 yen firmer, with the benchmark April 1998 contract ending up 1.5 yen at 208.5 yen per kg. The day's estimated volume was 5,485 lots.
"Following higher prices on the LME last Friday and the yen's dip, buying from local investors emerged from the outset," one trader said.
Activity ebbed later in the day, as most market players retreated to be sidelines amid a lack of fresh incentives and before the "Golden Week" holidays.
Japanese markets will be closed Tuesday for a national holiday.
